transcript:
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Dan Roman.
Some House Democrats, including the likely new Speaker in the next Congress, Hakeem Jeffries,
are calling on lawmakers to impeach Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth because of the way
the Pentagon has waged the U.S. war against Iran.
Jeffrey said Hegseth has abused his power and made the country less safe.
On CBS's Face the Nation, Arkansas Republican Congressman French Hill says he's willing
to listen to the case against Hegseth.
You know, I want to hear the debate on it to see if it merits impeachment versus some
other disciplinary action or action by the president if he's not getting the job done
in leading the Department of War.
That's the issue.
But Hill said ultimately America's handling of the war is up to the president as commander-in-chief.
The effort to remove Hegseth is being led by Kentucky Republican Housemember Thomas Massey.
The Trump administration says it plans to intervene in a Texas lawsuit against Planned
Parenthood.
NPR's Shondelice Duster reports the case centers on allegations the organization improperly
collected Medicaid payments.
In what is regarded as an attempt to shut down Planned Parenthood, attorneys for the
Justice Department filed a notice of appearance to the United States District Court for the
Northern District of Texas.
The notice follows days after Republicans, including Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton,
lost their seats to Democrats.
Paxton has been handling the years-long legal battle against Planned Parenthood.
The lawsuit accuses Planned Parenthood of Medicaid fraud, and the state is seeking to
recover $1.8 billion.
Susan Baker Manning, general counsel for Planned Parenthood, said in a statement that the organization
is going to "fight this every step of the way, including at trial."
NPR has reached out to the Justice Department for comment on the lawsuit, but has not received
a response.
Shondelice Duster, NPR News.
Pope Leo heads to Argentina on the second leg of his South American tour after visiting
Uruguay.
The pope became the first leader of the Catholic Church to visit Uruguay in nearly four decades,
where he attempted to remind people the Catholic Church is a big part of the country's identity
as a nation.
NPR's Kerry Khan has more on the pope's message there.
In the Capitol's historic football stadium last night, he spoke to his largest crowd.
He again made a push for more religion in public life.
He said society does offer plenty of institutions that do good, but he said none are a substitute
for God.
God's love is stronger than death, hatred, violence, war and sin, he said.
It's a message of joy.
The pope's visit to Argentina comes as the Catholic Church has criticized that nation's
austerity measures.
It's NPR.
Thousands of people gathered across France for a fourth weekend of demonstrations calling
for higher wages and better schools.
As Rebecca Rossman reports, the prime minister is expected to meet with union leaders and
business on Monday to come up with solutions and discuss the protests.
France's interior ministry says nearly 150,000 people gathered across the country Saturday,
a lower turnout than previous demonstrations.
A nationwide strike just two days ago drew more than half a million people.
Still, the French government says it's taking the protesters' grievances seriously.
On Monday, the French prime minister will meet with business leaders and workers to
discuss wages and living conditions.
The protests began in late September as a student movement, calling for better conditions
in schools, but have since evolved into a national push to address wider inequalities
across French society.
The demonstrations turned violent in mid-October.
Businesses were looted and set on fire, costing millions in damages.
Rebecca Rossman and Pierre-News Paris.
Israel's president has selected center-right political leader Ghazi Aizankat to try and
form a new government in Israel.
The decision is a setback to Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's efforts to try and stay
in office after the main political parties failed to gain a majority in the Israeli parliament.
Aizankat will now have up to six weeks to begin negotiations in an attempt to form a
coalition government with smaller political parties who won seats in last month's election.
President Isaac Herzog determined Aizankat has the best chance of forming a government.
I'm Dan Rullin, NPR News, Washington.
